Questions

How is a safe curve speed calculated?

V = √(15 · R · (e + f)), with V in mph, R the radius in feet, e the banking, and f the side friction. Engineers use the same relation to design curves.

How do I find a curve’s radius?

Tap any Arkansas curve on the RydAR map to see its radius. In the field, measure a chord C and the middle ordinate M; then R = C² ÷ 8M + M ÷ 2.

Why is unpaved slower?

Gravel and dirt grip less, so the formula uses 0.10 friction instead of 0.15.

Is this the advisory speed on the yellow sign?

Not necessarily. Posted advisory speeds are set by the road agency. Use this as a guide, and drive slower in rain, on gravel, or with worn tires.
